comment: Source-first semantic review of the two configured Roth82 premise declarations against the byte-pinned source text. Declaration and binder names were used only to locate the expanded propositions.

hcard : Fintype.card M = Fintype.card W.reason: The source explicitly contrasts the marriage model's equal numbers and complete matching with the later general matching model that may have unequal sides or unmatched agents.

assumption_equal_cardinality.reason: The expanded Lean proposition is equality of the finite cardinalities of the two sides. Roth's marriage-problem representation explicitly has equal numbers of men and women and excludes unmatched agents; the cardinality equality is therefore source-domain data, not a proof conclusion or an added regularity condition.
assumption_equal_cardinality.source_evidence: The byte-pinned passage states that the marriage problem has equal numbers of men and women and does not permit an outcome leaving an agent unmatched.
assumption_equal_cardinality.validator: Codex Roth82 semantic premise provenance auditor 2026-08-04

hfirst : ∀ w, w ≠ wstar → simple_report_.reason: Roth defines the equivalent simple misrepresentation by placing the partner produced by the arbitrary misrepresentation first, strictly above every other possible partner.

premises: hfirst : ∀ w, w ≠ wstar → simple_report_m w < simple_report_m wstar
assumption_simple_report_ranks_partner_f.reason: The expanded Lean proposition says that the partner obtained under the original misreport is strictly ranked above every distinct alternative by the associated simple report. This is exactly the construction Roth specifies before Lemma 1, not a supplied proof of Lemma 1's same-partner conclusion.
assumption_simple_report_ranks_partner_f.source_evidence: The byte-pinned passage defines the equivalent simple report by making the partner obtained under the arbitrary report the reporting man's most preferred match.
assumption_simple_report_ranks_partner_f.validator: Codex Roth82 semantic premise provenance auditor 2026-08-04
